entry.event: start

Patient Thor Axlung, 67-year-old male with history of smoking (quit 2018, 40 pack-years), COPD, and hypertension, presents with persistent cough lasting 3 weeks following a recent COVID-19 infection. No fever, hemoptysis, or significant weight loss reported. Physical exam: Clear lungs, no distress. Ordered chest CT to evaluate.
CT Chest: 3.2 cm mass in left upper lobe with associated hilar adenopathy. No evidence of distant metastasis. Recommend further evaluation with biopsy. Referred to oncology for consultation.

event.name: Malignant neoplasm of upper lobe, right bronchus or lung

entry.event: Biopsy from left upper lobe mass: Moderately differentiated squamous cell carcinoma. NGS panel results: ALK rearrangement positive. EGFR: Negative. ROS1: Negative. BRAF: Negative. MET exon 14: Negative. RET: Negative. NTRK: Negative. KRAS: Negative. ERBB2 (HER2): Negative. NRG1: Negative. PD-L1 expression: Low (TPS 20%). Recommend staging PET/CT.
PET/CT: Hypermetabolic left upper lobe nodule (SUV 14.2), hilar lymph nodes involved, no distant metastases. Staging: cT2bN1M0 (Stage IIA). Proceed to surgical evaluation.
Value: 4.5 ng/mL (normal <5.0)

event.name: Thoracoscopic left upper lobectomy with lymph node dissection

entry.event: Performed left upper lobectomy and mediastinal lymph node dissection. Pathology: pT2bN1M0 squamous cell carcinoma, margins clear. Patient tolerated procedure well, discharged on POD 5.

Post-op CT stable, no evidence of recurrence. No adjuvant therapy recommended given stage and performance status (ECOG 0). Continue surveillance every 3-6 months. Patient reports good recovery, minimal dyspnea managed with inhalers for COPD.
Value: 3.8 ng/mL
New 2.5 cm nodule in left lower lobe, suspicious for recurrence. Mild hilar enlargement. Recommend PET/CT for further staging. Patient noted mild dyspnea and 5 lb weight loss since last visit.

Recurrent disease: Left lower lobe mass 6.5 x 4.8 cm (SUV 18.6), bilateral pulmonary nodules, hilar nodes, and hypermetabolic bone lesions in T10 vertebra and right rib. No brain involvement on concurrent MRI. Staging: cT3N2M1b (Stage IV). Refer back to oncology for systemic therapy options.
Value: 12.3 ng/mL (elevated)

FNA from mediastinal nodes: Positive for squamous cell carcinoma, ALK rearrangement confirmed via FISH. Updated NGS: ALK positive; all other markers (EGFR, ROS1, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK, KRAS, ERBB2, NRG1) negative. PD-L1 TPS 20% (low). Recommend initiation of systemic therapy.

Initiated pembrolizumab + carboplatin/paclitaxel for metastatic ALK-positive squamous NSCLC. Vitals: BP 140/85, HR 92, SpO2 94%, Weight 78 kg, BMI 25.1. Patient counseled on side effects. ALK inhibitors like alectinib considered for future if progression. Follow-up imaging in 2 months.

After 2 cycles of therapy: Partial response noted on interim CT (mass reduced to 4.2 cm). However, patient reports grade 2 neuropathy and fatigue. Dose reduction implemented. Continue regimen; reassess after 2 more cycles. No new mets on bone scan.
Value: 7.6 ng/mL (decreasing)

Completed 4 cycles with stable disease. Ongoing symptoms: Progressive cough and 6 lb weight loss. Vitals stable. Plan for restaging PET/CT. Discussed potential switch to alectinib if progression, given ALK status from prior pathology.
Prescribed for COPD management, 2 puffs as needed.
Prescribed for hypertension, 10 mg daily.

Reviewed current medications during tumor board referral preparation. Patient on Albuterol inhaler for COPD (as needed) and Lisinopril 10 mg daily for hypertension. No changes recommended at this time; continue alongside oncology treatments. No reported allergies or interactions with ongoing pembrolizumab and chemo.

Restaging PET/CT: Stable left lower lobe mass (4.0 cm, SUV 12.4), persistent bone lesions with mild progression in rib. No new sites. Staging remains cT3N2M1b (Stage IV). Recommend tumor board review for therapy adjustment.
Value: 8.2 ng/mL
